primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators IV
primary_antecedent.scope: Complete geometric condition-Psi preparation, including arbitrary smooth multipliers, all three formulations and the exact compact complex normal form.

source_correspondence: The directed sign test uses strict endpoint signs with no assumption about isolated or finite-order zeros. One-dimensional complex bicharacteristics retain the exact real tangent condition.

The full locally Lipschitz flow is obtained by contraction and continuous dependence. The nearest-point normal criterion is proved in both directions with a uniform discrete distance estimate; no external viability theorem is substituted.

The closed forward saturation is proved invariant. At regular zeros its normals are nonnegative multiples of the differential; at singular zeros the two fields agree. This proves the complete sign-transfer lemma on C2 manifolds.
An ordinary compact Hamiltonian tube is constructed from exact earlier prescribed coordinates, finite continuation, full symplectic pairings and compact injectivity.

Triangular changes preserve simultaneous time and sign reversal. A general positive-determinant matrix is reduced by a transverse projection, with all coefficients and singular-zero field identities written explicitly.
Complex multiplier invariance is proved without homogeneity assumptions, near a characteristic point or an embedded compact one-dimensional interval.

The lower-limit minimization includes nearby trajectories, endpoint limits and all restricted derivatives. The positive-length limiting interval is a one-dimensional characteristic; a zero-length limit is a characteristic point.
Homogeneity of the original symbol excludes radial, reverse-orientation and periodic returns of the limiting cosphere curve, even when the offending multiplier is nonhomogeneous.

Exact homogeneous extensions along an embedded cosphere interval prove equivalence of all three condition-Psi formulations. The point test is reduced to one of the two elementary real/imaginary choices.

The full compact complex normal form preserves the given parameter, exact pointwise curve, multiplier degree and nonzero last momentum. Injectivity of the cosphere projection is shown to imply regularity.

The common-domain complex division is patched by a finite partition in time. Every canonical pair, the global flow inverse and the homogeneous degrees are retained. The imaginary part is exactly independent of temporal momentum.

Restricted flatness is converted directly to full flatness by division in the original real-part tube, including the nonzero complex temporal derivative. No unproved preservation under an intermediate real hypersurface change is assumed.
The necessity companion uses these tubes and sign equivalences to prove necessity of condition Psi. The solvability companion supplies the exact adjoint estimate used in that argument.
